results.question: What are the main ingredients of a Colombian ajiaco?
results.reply_text:
Main ingredients of a Colombian Ajiaco (Ajiaco Bogotano):

Chicken (usually whole or pieces) – the protein base of the soup.
Three varieties of potatoes – typically papa criolla, papa pastos (or papa sabanera), and papa roja (or papa amarilla), which give the soup its distinctive texture and flavor.
Corn on the cob (elote or maíz) – adds sweetness and a creamy texture when cooked.
Guascas – an aromatic herb native to the Andes, essential for the characteristic flavor.
Capsicum (optional) – small green chili peppers for a mild spicy note.
Cilantro (or culantro) – fresh herbs for garnish and additional aroma.
Cream (crema de leche) – stirred in at the end to enrich the broth.
Capers – provide a salty, briny contrast.
Avocado – served on the side or sliced into the soup for freshness and creaminess.
White rice – traditionally served alongside to soak up the broth.
Salt and pepper – to taste.

These components together create the hearty, comforting soup that is iconic in Bogotá and throughout Colombia.
